data.name: Federal Reserve Chairmen
data.shortDescription: Federal Reserve leaders from 1914 onward with key details.
data.longDescription: Federal Reserve leaders from 1914 onward, with exact service dates, first appointing presidents and their parties, birth details, ages at entry and departure, and tenure lengths.
notes: One row per substantive leader in the conventional sequence beginning with Charles Hamlin: governors (active executive officers) of the Federal Reserve Board, followed by chairs of the Board of Governors. Reappointments are combined. Treasury secretaries who chaired ex officio and separate acting or pro tempore appointments are not numbered as additional leaders.

William Gibbs McAdoo was not an acting predecessor to Hamlin. As Treasury secretary, he chaired ex officio from December 23, 1913, to December 15, 1918, overlapping Hamlin and Harding. That separate office and its other holders are outside this sequence.

Service dates follow the Federal Reserve Board membership table, with Eccles's governor and chair service combined. The table does not consistently include interim service; these dates are its published boundaries, not a complete accounting of all acting appointments. Known biography discrepancies are recorded in row notes.

Federal Reserve biographies establish birth years and places where available. Full birth dates are supplemented by the named archival, institutional, or secondary birthDateSource. Only factual data are reproduced.

Appointing presidents through Yellen are checked against CRS Table 1; Powell and Warsh use Federal Reserve appointment announcements. Presidential numbers and parties are checked against the presidential list and House party history.
